Chances at Proxima are zero and building a colony there would be a waste of time and resources.

At A and B, there are actual realistic habitable zones. A hypothetical colony would have a nice view with two suns. Though one of them would appear only 0.1% to 1% as bright as the other.
Yes, the companion star would (seen from a hypothetical Nova Terra) probably look more like a very bright star (brighter than we can see from earth) than like a small sun.

The "1%" star would be still very much brighter than the moon. Probably equivalent to the dispersed light of the main star just after setting behind the horizon (assuming there is an atmosphere similar to ours).

Proxima is indeed, as is typical for such a small star, a flare star (meaning that it usually rather dim but has unpredictably irregulr, short episodes when it becomes much bright and gives off huge sunflames.

If mankind, or a portion of it, wants to take a chance at Proxima B, they'd have to dig in and live underground.

This is why we need to embrace the idea of climate change and find ways to control it.

When we set out to colonize other planets, there won't be a "Perfect" planet that will suit us. We evolved on Earth and finding a 100% Earth like planet isn't going to be possible. We are going to have a handful of choices around Alpha Centauri or Proxima Centauri and at best, we'll probably have something as comfortable as Mars or Europa.

Which brings me back to my point about climate change. Earth is our training wheels. If we can't figure out how to do something as simple as keeping our planet within a few degrees of changing, there's no fucking way we are going to be able to terraform a planet when we need to do it as a matter of survival.

I don't give a fuck about the politics of climate change. I don't give a fuck if it is natural or man-caused. I don't give a fuck if it's fake news or whatever. It doesn't matter. We need to act as if it is real regardless, because the ability to change the climate is a tool we are going to need once we land on a world which is hostile to life. This is true regardless of this conspiracy theory or that fear-mongering argument.
